newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-INJURY COULD RULE SCHOLES OUT OF FRANCE CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURY COULD RULE SCHOLES OUT OF FRANCE CLASH.

text.p: Paul Scholes, who made an impressive full debut for England against Italy, could miss Saturday's match against France because of a hamstring injury.
"It will be a shame for him if he doesn't play," coach Glenn Hoddle said on the eve of the Tournoi de France clash in Montpellier.
"Paul played very well on Wednesday, for me he was the best player on the pitch and I wanted to look at how he played together with Alan Shearer.
"But he has picked up a slight hamstring strain and we won't know until tomorrow whether he will be fit or not."
The 22-year-old Manchester United forward made England's opening goal against the Italians in Nantes and then scored himself to seal the 2-0 victory.
Hoddle will delay naming his side until he knows whether midfielder Robert Lee recovers from a foot injury he picked up in last week's World Cup qualifier against Poland.
"If he is 100 per cent he will play," said Hoddle who added that Paul Gascoigne was fully fit after suffering a gashed thigh against Poland.
Shearer, who was not risked against the Italians, said he was desperate to play against France.

"The coach has explained to me why he didn't play me against South Africa or Italy and, while I understand the reasons, I am disappointed to miss any game. I have told him that but it's up to him to pick the team for the occasion."

Hoddle said: "I know how Alan feels but sometimes when you have a jewel in the crown, you have to protect it. I thought he played perhaps his best international match against Poland. He worked unbelievably hard, especially in the first half.

"It is easy for fatigue to set into the muscles after a hard game like that and it would have been very annoying if he had picked up a silly injury against Italy which would have kept him out for the next few games."
